LESSON: A gate verdict of 'excluded' (declared-ahead) is not the same as 'refuse' (a live-measured incompleteness) -- both fail closed to the same allowlist outcome, but only one represents an actual live REFUSE observation. Don't assume a known-partial county (like Caldwell) will supply a REFUSE case without checking; it may correctly be excluded instead.

A LIKE-prefix predicate against parcel_record_cell (place_key LIKE '48491:%') times out even at 60s under this table's scale; a range predicate (place_key >= '48491:' AND place_key < '48492:') on the same column is sargable and returns near-instantly.

The purpose-built gate-rail-cli.mjs (paged, designed for scale) survives contention that raw ad hoc SQL does not -- but running it LOCALLY without --apply only proves the DATA state; it does not persist anything. The real Cloud Run job with --apply is a separate, required step for any flip to actually take effect.

A field deliberately kept identical across two backends for response-shape parity (this card's own `source` field, kept as 'well-fact'/'special-district-fact'/'tx_city_boundary' regardless of which adapter served it) is the WRONG field to probe when verifying a cutover live -- use a field the new adapter actually owns (sourceAdapter, a refusal code prefix, or a basis-string signature).

gcloud run services describe can return stale, inconsistent state for the first 1-3 calls immediately after a deploy -- re-verify with repeated fresh reads until they agree before trusting traffic/revision state for anything load-bearing.

In a genuinely shared doc_repo working directory (multiple concurrent agent sessions committing to the same local main branch), always re-fetch and diff immediately before writing to a shared artifact path -- a competing write can already be sitting in your working tree from another session's commit, indistinguishable from your own until you check.
